title: Which record owns the scan of STEGO's own Go modules for known vulnerabilities?
description: The workflows check STEGO's own dependencies: go mod verify and govulncheck in checks.yml and runtime-library.yml, and vulnerability-scan.yml (ST-ASR-TOOL06), which scans every Go module on main each week. No design record asks for this, so no test of it can be a proof: the test of the module list in scripts/test_release_publishing.py names no record. Options: (a) a new rule of ST-STD-TRUST: every Go module of STEGO MUST be verified against its go.sum and scanned for known vulnerabilities by each check of the module and on main each week, and a reachable known vulnerability MUST fail the check; its test is the module list test; (b) a UC requirement of an Assuring use case; (c) keep it as tooling with no proof. Recommendation: (a): it is an engineering rule for STEGO's own code, as the rules of ST-STD-TRUST are, and it holds the scan to every module, also one added later.

title: Where does an archetype's example content come from, and which settings must an author supply?
description: ST-DECL-UC01-R01 and R04 say each archetype supplies the smallest example content that checking accepts, and R05 says an empty scaffold names every setting the author must supply. Today the scaffolds of rpc-service and browser-service are refused: rpc-service needs the grpc-processes settings processes and proto_files, a proto file and a process factory package (factory/rpc.go) that imports the generated packages by the module path; browser-service needs a distinct api_prefix. The Archetype entity (ST-SUP-EN03) has no field that holds example content, and a component schema marks as required both settings the declaration must give and settings that only the running service gets (such as connection_string of postgres-adapter and issuer of jwt-auth), so checking cannot tell which settings an author must supply. Options: (a) add to the Archetype an example content field (files under the archetype folder and the settings to write into the declaration, with the module path as a placeholder), and mark in a component schema each setting the declaration must give, so that checking refuses its absence and init can name it; (b) keep the example content in Declaring's code, one case per archetype; (c) narrow R01, R04 and R05 to archetypes that can be empty, such as rest-crud. Recommendation: (a), since the UC01 notes say the archetype supplies its example content, and a registry change then needs no change to STEGO's code. Until then UC01-R01, R04-T01, R05 and the flow test stay not automated; rest-crud, which can be empty, already passes as written.

title: Which step of Record what a service was built from fulfills that apply writes the record inside the service's repo?
description: ST-GEN-UC01-R05 says that apply MUST write the record inside the service's repo, beside the code it generated. Only the step ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S02 (the service author commits the record with the generated code) fulfills it, and that step invokes no command, so no technical record can build the requirement, although ST-GEN-UC01-R05-T01 is automated and passes. Options: (a) ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S01, which invokes Apply a plan (ST-GEN-CMD01), also fulfills ST-GEN-UC01-R05, and S02 keeps it too; (b) S02 also invokes Apply a plan; (c) the requirement stays proved and not built. Recommendation: (a), since apply is what writes the record in the repo and the commit only shows it.

title: What system receives the audit-sink messages of a generated service?
description: The audit-sink port is bound by the platform (ST-GEN-INV37, ST-DECL-EN10) and the generated NewWorker refuses to start without it (ST-SUP-RC18-OC30-T04), but no component, runtime package or setting gives the process an implementation of audit.Sink. So the worker mode of a service on the runtime data path cannot register the destination audit-sink. Until this is decided, the generated service gives the worker a held sink: each delivery is refused as transient, so each audit message and anchor stays in the outbox, is retried with backoff and is never lost (the destination must land, ST-SUP-RP05-LC14), and the worker mode logs at its start that the port is not bound. Options: (a) the runtime gives an HTTPS sink, reached by fixed settings (an endpoint and a credential file), that sends each event and anchor with its event ID as the idempotency key; (b) the runtime gives a sink that writes each event and anchor as a log record of the telemetry runtime, which the platform collects; (c) the platform runs its own reader of the outbox, and the service registers no audit-sink destination. Recommendation: (a): the sink is outside the service with no way back (ST-SUP-RP05-LC08), a delivery is idempotent by the event ID, and a local stand-in keeps the contract for tests.

title: At what stage does oidc-auth enter the registry, when an alpha component must not provide auth-provider?
description: The registry record ST-SUP-RC37 gives oidc-auth the stage alpha with the sunset 2027-04-30, and oidc-auth provides the port auth-provider. ST-SUP-INV03 refuses a component that is not ga and provides a port that a ga component provides, and jwt-auth and rh-sso-auth are ga and provide auth-provider; so the registry refuses to load with oidc-auth at alpha. ST-STD-TRUST-R01 refuses a generator with no shipped component, so the generator cannot be registered either. The generator (internal/generator/oidcauth), its declaration (internal/generator/oidcauth/testdata/component.yaml) and the end-to-end test of a service with oidc-auth are written and pass when the declaration is shipped at ga; rh-sso-auth on the runtime data path, a configuration of oidc-auth, ships now. Options: (a) oidc-auth enters at ga: its verification is the runtime verifier (ST-SUP-RP13), which had its security review in PR #144, and rh-sso-auth, a ga component, is a configuration of it; the owner waives the evidence of ST-SUP-UC05-R04 and R05 for this entry, or names what to record first; (b) oidc-auth stays alpha and provides a port of its own, and the runtime wiring takes a service that declares it as its auth provider, which changes how the auth-provider binding works (ST-GEN-INV37); (c) ST-SUP-INV03 admits an alpha component on a port of a ga component when the declaration accepts it by name (ST-SUP-UC04-R02). Recommendation: (a): the store path is being removed, so there is no experiment period to protect, and the code that decides each token is already the reviewed runtime verifier. The change after the decision is to move the declaration to registry/components/oidc-auth at ga, register the generator in cmd/stego, and set ST-SUP-RC37-OC01-T01 to OC04-T01 to automated.
